## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mastery of deployment strategies in large Kubernetes environments, emphasizing real-world constraints, traffic control, observability, and DR.

## Key Concepts
- Canary and blue/green deployments
- Traffic shaping with service mesh (Istio/Linkerd)
- Readiness/Liveness probes, PodDisruptionBudget
- Rollbacks, error budgets, observability
- DR planning, RBAC

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 25%
      maxSurge: 25%
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payments
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payments
        image: myrepo/payments:canary-1
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure canary success and trigger rollback?
- What metrics and alerting would you configure?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical understanding of Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, with real-world constraints like DNS-based destinations and in-cluster services. Candidates must translate security intent into concrete policy syntax and a verifiable test plan.

## Key Concepts

- NetworkPolicy scope (namespaced, podSelector, namespaceSelector)
- Egress rules, DNS-based destinations vs IP blocks
- Testing strategy with temporary pods and DNS/port checks
- Rollback and safety checks for production readiness

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-payments-egress
  namespace: payments
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-service
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - dnsName: vendor.example.com
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: redis
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 6379
```

> Note: dnsName is supported by some CNIs (e.g., Calico). If unsupported, substitute with exact IP blocks after validating DNS resolution in a test pod.

## Follow-up Questions

- What are the risks of DNS-based policies and DNS TTL caching?
- How would you automate rollback in CI/CD when a policy blocks legitimate traffic?

```javascript
  name: app

        vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, violations
- Rego rules for Pod security, matching exclusions

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (illustrative)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8spodsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sPodSecurityPolicy
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8spodsecurity
      violation[violation] {
        input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
        some container
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (illustrative)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sPodSecurityPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-ps
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    excludedNamespaces: ["kube-system"]
  parameters: {}
```

- How would you monitor violations in CI/CD?

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical use of Indexed Jobs for deterministic shard processing, with concrete verification steps.

## Key Concepts
- Indexed Jobs
- Downward API POD_INDEX
- Idempotent shard processing
- Kubernetes job monitoring

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: batch-job
spec:
  completions: 8
  parallelism: 8
  completionMode: Indexed
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: my/worker:latest
        # POD_INDEX maps to shard
        env:
        - name: SHARD
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.annotations['batch.kubernetes.io/index']
      restartPolicy: Never
```

- How do you test idempotency guarantees across restarts?

## Why This Is Asked
Auditing is central to security and compliance; this tests practical setup of an external webhook sink with a canary rollout and safe rollback procedures.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Audit policy configuration
- AuditSink and webhook sink implementation
- Canary rollout strategy and rollback mechanisms
- Retry logic, exponential backoff, and rate limiting

## Code Example
```yaml
# audit-policy.yaml
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
rules:
- level: Metadata
  resources:
  - group: ""
    resources: ["pods","configmaps","secrets"]
```

```yaml
# audit-sink.yaml (canary sink)
apiVersion: auditregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: AuditSink
metadata:
  name: audit-sink-canary
spec:
  webhook:
    clientConfig:
      service:
        name: audit-webhook-service
        namespace: audit-system
        path: "/audit"
      timeout: 30s
    throttle:
      qps: 10
      burst: 20
    retryBackoff:
      base: 1s
      max: 30s
```

```bash
# Apply audit policy and canary sink
kubectl apply -f audit-policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f audit-sink-canary.yaml

# Generate test events
kubectl run test-pod --image=nginx --restart=Never
kubectl delete pod test-pod

# Verify SIEM ingestion and proceed to full rollout
curl -X POST https://siem-endpoint/audit/check
kubectl apply -f audit-sink-full.yaml
```

```yaml

kind: LimitRange
```
